title: cc_registry_session_resolution_v1
description: M5 deferred scaffold: the current verifier rejects every caller-supplied available result; a positive producer must be implemented and qualified at P0.7/P0.8. This is the future producer contract for effective per-definition metadata. It is frozen, not executor-selectable, because the question it answers — 'is the metadata this definition declares the metadata actually in force?' — is exactly the question a plugin-authored producer or a model self-report cannot answer about itself. A definition whose frontmatter fails to parse loads with empty metadata and says nothing about it at the point of use, so re-reading the YAML would report the declaration and call it the projection. A row is therefore valid only when the HOST generated it: raw `claude plugin list --json` and `claude plugin details` records, plus a real session invocation/debug record that resolves the same component to the same plugin ID or --plugin-dir root, the same session, and the effective model/tools/effort in force there. Every row in one snapshot must share one session and one source root; a row correlated to a different session or a different root is describing a different world. When the host cannot emit those fields, the honest snapshot records status 'unavailable' with the exact facts and NO rows, and the verifier exits 42 so the caller can tell 'blocked' from 'invalid'. This shape carries the ATTESTATION answer only: whether the declarations parse and project their own fields is a separate question with a separate answer, and verify-effective-snapshot.sh --accept-unavailable reports the two side by side so an honest 'unavailable' can be accepted as a capability observation without ever reading as 'the declared metadata is in force'. Read by verify-effective-snapshot.sh.

producer.description: Who generated the rows. 'generated_by' is a const, not an enum: the only accepted answer is the host itself. A plugin-authored script, a model report, or a YAML re-read is rejected by name in verify-effective-snapshot.sh so the rejection is legible rather than a schema miss.

raw_records.description: The host-generated bytes the rows were read out of. Each is a repo-relative path with a raw digest; a snapshot that cites no raw record is a summary.

resolution.description: The single world every row must belong to.

availability.description: Whether this host can emit the frozen producer at all. 'unavailable' is a legitimate, reviewable answer and requires the exact facts that make it so; it is not a licence to substitute a different producer.

rows.description: One closed row per definition. Empty exactly when availability is 'unavailable' — a partially filled row set would be the substitution this contract exists to refuse.

effective.description: What the host reports as in force — not what the file declares. A null here is a field the host did not report, and it fails: 'unknown' and 'as declared' are the two answers this contract exists to keep apart.

correlation.description: Where in the host's own output this row was read. A row with no locatable origin is a claim about the host, not a record from it.
